title: What this is
text:
One of you is the Dungeon Master, the DM, who describes the world and plays everyone in it. The rest of you each run one character. There is no board and nobody wins.

The DM says what is happening. You say what your character does. When it is not obvious how that turns out, someone rolls a twenty-sided die. Then round it goes again.

title: The one roll
text:
Roll the d20, add a number from your sheet, and try to equal or beat a target.

Trying something hard is a check, against a number the DM picks. Hitting something is an attack, against its Armour Class. Resisting something is a saving throw.

With Advantage, roll two and keep the higher. With Disadvantage, keep the lower. Both at once cancel out.

title: A fight starts with initiative
text:
Everyone rolls a d20 and adds their Dexterity modifier. Tap each name on my screen and enter the total. The DM does the same for the monsters.

Highest goes first, and that order holds for the whole fight. I keep it. If two tie, the DM picks, and Wins ties tells me who.

title: A round
text: A round is about six seconds, and everyone gets one turn in it. Press the button when a turn ends and I call the next name. After the last name I start the next round and count it.

title: Your turn
text:
You may move, up to your Speed, before and after you act.

You get one action: attack, cast a spell, dash, dodge, hide, help, and so on.

You get a bonus action only if something on your sheet says it uses one.

Once a round, on anyone's turn, you get one reaction. Your book lists what each of these can be.

title: Hitting and hurting
text:
To attack, roll the d20 and add your attack bonus. Equal or beat the target's Armour Class and you hit: roll the damage.

Tap the name of whoever was hurt, then Damage, and enter the number. For characters I take it off the sheet, temporary hit points first. The DM keeps the monsters' hit points, and I show them to nobody else.

title: Conditions
text:
Blinded, prone, poisoned and the rest are conditions. Tap a name, then Condition, and I pin the word to them and say it again when their turn comes.

I keep the words only. What each one does is in your book, under Conditions. Hold the button and ask, and I shall find the page.

title: Concentration
text:
Some spells last only while the caster concentrates, and a caster can hold one such spell at a time. Mark them as concentrating.

When they take damage they roll a Constitution save to keep it. The number to beat is 10, or half the damage rounded down, whichever is higher. I work it out and ask whether it held.

title: At 0 hit points
text:
A character at 0 hit points is down and out cold. At the start of each of their turns they roll a plain d20: 10 or more passes, less fails.

Three passes and they are stable. Three fails and they die. A 1 counts as two fails. A 20 puts them back up on 1 hit point. Any healing ends it and wakes them.

Being hit while down is a failed save. I count the boxes.

title: Resting
text:
A short rest is about an hour: spend hit dice to heal. That one is yours to work out from your sheet.

A long rest is a night's sleep. I put hit points and spell slots back. Under the 2024 rules every hit die comes back; under the 2014 rules, half of them.

title: What I do not do
text:
I hold names and numbers. I do not hold what a spell, a class feature, a monster or a magic item does. For those I tell you which entry to read in your own book, and Lookup will open it if that book has been loaded.

And I never tell the DM how to rule. I have opinions. I keep them.
